summary: phpBB is a bulletin board software solution designed for hosting structured web forums. It allows you to set up threaded discussions to communicate with a specific community or run a central website. The platform provides standard discussion board functionality built on the PHP language.
goodFor: This is a suitable choice if you need a traditional, self-hosted forum platform to manage community discussions under the GPL-2.0 licence. It fits administrators who prefer classic bulletin board layouts over modern real-time chat interfaces.
watchOut: The project exhibits steady rather than rapid activity, and you may find that it faces strong competition from more active or feature-rich alternative community platforms. Customisation and maintenance of older PHP architectures can also introduce administrative overhead.
deployNotes: As a PHP application, you will typically need to provision a separate relational database like MySQL or PostgreSQL, alongside a web server such as Nginx or Apache. Persistent storage is required for user-uploaded content, and you will need to handle TLS termination via a reverse proxy.
